description.narrative:
The intervention aims at contributing to democratic, credible, inclusive and peaceful national elections, planned to be held in Ethiopia in 2020. Expected results are as follows: - that the electoral management body (EMB) becomes capable, transparent and credible in organising the national elections in Ethiopia; - pre-conditions are created for inclusive, transparent and credible elections; - that the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE), can ensure inclusive participation throughout the elections, amongst women, youth, and the different ethnic groups in all regions of Ethiopia, to contribute to a credible and inclusive electoral process.
Specific excpected results of the intervention are as follows: 1. The transparency, efficiency and inclusiveness of the electoral operations are enhanced through the operational support provided to the National Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) 1.1 Capacity of the permanent electoral officials enhanced to professionally deliver planning and implementation of gender-sensitive electoral legal reform 1.2 Professional, transparent and inclusive electoral operations supported 1.3 Voter registration operations are enhanced promoting inclusive participation of youth, women and disadvantaged groups 1.4 Inclusive and transparent Results Management System (RMS) enhanced 1.5 Procurement services availed 1.6 Post-electoral support provided to assess transparency, credibility and gender equality of the process
2. The capacity of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) in conducting public outreach and external communication, including engagement with media and other key electoral stakeholders, is enhanced 2.1 NEBE communication and external relations capacity improved with a specific attention to conflict and gender-specific messaging 2.2 All electoral stakeholders informed and trained, and Media Centre established to encourage conflict- and gender-sensitive messaging 2.3 Civic/Voter education planned and well-coordinated ensuring inclusive participation of women and youth both as coordinators and beneficiaries
3. The capacity of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) and other key stakeholders to identify, manage and respond to electoral violence enhanced 3.1 NEBE and its partners capacity to prevent electoral violence enhanced through a monitoring and early warning and response system (EVERS) 3.2 Electoral dispute resolution system is more effective and rights-based 3.3 Security forces are trained and sensitized to election security good practices

Objective 1: The transparency, efficiency and inclusiveness of the electoral operations are enhanced through the operational support provided to the National Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
With training, consultations and material support, the program supported NEBE in enhancing its capacity to run elections more transparently, efficiently, and inclusively. The improvements in voter registration, material procurement, and gender-sensitive training aligned well with the programs objectives. For instance, by improving voter registration the accuracy and efficiency also improved. Furthermore, by providing ballots and forms, this contributed to transparency and efficiency.
However, challenges such as the incomplete implementation of the aims targeting inclusiveness for vulnerable group limited the success of the program. For instance, the UN Women production of a documentary on women in elections and the development for procedures for IDPs to vote were both not fully implemented.
To conclude, the program successfully worked to increase transperancy and efficency, while the objective for inclusiveness was not fully successfull.
Objective 2: The capacity of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) in conducting public outreach and external communication, including engagement with media and other key electoral stakeholders, is enhanced.
The project fostered a collaborative, multi-stakeholder framework for electoral support. In fact, the project managed to involve more than 400 internal and external electoral stakeholders. This helped to increase trust in the electoral process and expose different actors to one anothers experiences.
However, challenges remained in fully enhancing NEBEs capacity for public outreach and external communication, particularly in terms of media engagement and the awareness of electoral information. In the light of low media scrutiny during the national election in 2020 and the terminal reports assessment that more targeted efforts to the media was needed, Sida deems that a more holistic approach of NEBEs work would have been more successful. To conclude, by ensuring that all actors are equipped with necessary information to engage effectively in the electoral process, the project would be better positioned to promote transparency, inclusiveness, and accountability in future elections.
Objective 3: The capacity of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) and other key stakeholders to identify, manage and respond to electoral violence enhanced.
To begin with, the context for this objective was highly challenging due to rapidly changing political, security, and electoral conditions. This impacted dramatically the elections and the project implementation. Security issues affected multiple regions during the implementation period, and elections were only held in June 2021, although areas like Tigray and Benishangul Gumuz were unable to participate due to ongoing conflict. This led to frequent changes in work plans and delays in preparations for NEBE and other electoral stakeholders, including civil society and political parties.
Furthermore, although the program completed a conflict mapping, the terminal report by UNDP assesses that the actions to prevent and mitigate electoral violence should have been reassessed. While NEBE led the coordination of national electoral efforts, there are other bodies responsible for security management in Ethiopia. The report concluded that NEBE may not be the most appropriate body to gather, hold and respond to security-related information. The report assessed that it may have been advantageous to re-evaluate this project component at an earlier stage.
Due to these reasons, Sida concludes that the objective is partly achieved. NEBE showed a capacity to respond to increased violence that threatened elections. However, to fully identify, manage and respond to electoral violence, SIDA believes that NEBE mandate would then have to be to be modified.
Conclusion:
The final evaluation report conducted in late 2021 concludeded that 88% of the stakeholders were satisfied with the results of the program. Furthermore, the evaluation also assessed that one year before the end of the program, 45% of the goals were achieved, 35% were partly achieved, 8% were yet to be implemented, 12% were not achieved.
Based on the evaluation report, together with the individual assessment of each objective, Sida concludes that the program was successful with many of its goals achieved or partly achieved. The results of SEEDS programs is therefore viewed as satisfactory.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
